newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FAI MBS issue oversubscribed - Westpac.
newsitem.headline: FAI MBS issue oversubscribed - Westpac.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp said on Friday that FAI First Mortgage Pty Ltd's Residential Mortgage Trust (FAIFM/RMT) received strong market support for its A$240 million of mortgage-backed bonds resulting in the oversubscrition of both tranches.
The issue comprised A$228 million senior bonds and A$12 million subordinated bonds, priced on Thursday at 25 and 34 basis points respectively over the one month bank bill swap (BBSW) rate.

The senior bonds carry a AAA rating from Standard and Poor's and have an expected average life of 4.4 years, while the subordinated bonds carry a AA-minus rating and have an expected average life of six years.

"In what has been a weak market during the past six to eight weeks the issue was well-received by a broad range of institutional and corporate investors in Victoria, New South Wales and Queensland," Westpac Corporate Finance director Sean McElduff said in a statement.

"The strong demand for the issue was reflective of investor perceptions as to the high quality of the mortgage pool which is comprised of a large number of investment property owners with low debt servicing ratios and high net worth," McElduff said.
Westpac said FAIFM/RMT had experienced significantly improved pricing since its debt mortgage backed securities issue in August last year.
"While RMT2 has achieved better pricing in the capital markets than RMT1, FAIFM's growth over the last year means that cheaper offshore funding opportunities are now viable for FAIFM," it said.

"The RMT issue brings total MBS issurance for the period January to July this year ot A$4.25 billion. This is just under the total amount of MBS issued during 1996 which was A$4.7 billion," the bank said.
